newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends flat as dollar supply rises.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends flat as dollar supply rises.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed between 348-354 per dollar, in a narrower spread than the 340-356 in the morning, after foreign currency supply rose on profit taking in light interbank trade, dealers said.
"More companies offered dollars, which they have retained during the lev slide last week on expectation of a further fall," a bank dealer said.
"It seems that dollar buying has met resistance near 355 levs and probably, the dollar would idle around these levels for the time being," another trader said.
The central bank had probably absorbed part of the rise in dollar supply, consolidating the lev near 350 per dollar, traders said. Central bank officials declined comment.
The lev fell to 395 per dollar from 272-275 last week before the central bank (BNB) said on Friday it had agreed to coordinated action with commercial banks to prevent further sharp falls in the lev.
Details of the agreement were not available.

Monday's news that the government and the central bank had accepted the currency board plan for Bulgaria proposed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) did not have any impact on trade on the local forex market, dealers said.

"The market was not moved because it is still not clear to which foreign currency and at what exchange rate the lev will be pegged and how we will trade, maybe in a corridor along the pegged rate," a third dealer said.
Currency boards, usually pegging the local currency to the dollar, have been used to defeat hyperinflation and restore confidence in countries like Argentina, Estonia and Lithuania.
The parliament has yet to debate whether to peg the lev to the dollar or the German mark. Germany is Bulgaria's biggest investor and trade partner.

Announcing acceptance of the IMF plan, Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said on Monday the cabinet planned to invite an IMF mission for technical preparation of the currency board system that would match money in circulation to the level of the country's foreign currency reserves. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
